title: Notification payload templates
blurb: Shape the JSON a notification channel posts. Open Edit Payload on a channel tab and write your own body with variables such as {{level}} and {{message}}; leave it blank for the built-in payload.

title: HTTPS on the Sencho instance
blurb: Terminate TLS on Sencho itself when you are not using a reverse proxy. Point SENCHO_TLS_CERT_FILE and SENCHO_TLS_KEY_FILE at a mounted certificate and key and set SENCHO_PUBLIC_URL to https, and Pilot agents enroll over a confidential tunnel.

title: Sealed private-registry credentials
blurb: Credentials for private images travel sealed to compatible remote nodes, even over plain HTTP. Sencho pins each node's sealing key on first use; use Reset seal pin under Settings → Nodes after a rebuild.

title: Health-gated rollouts across the fleet
blurb: Choose what a Git-managed Blueprint rollout does when a target's health check fails: observe (the default), pause, retry once, stop, or roll that target back. Each node reports the health of the stack it runs, so a remote target settles on a real verdict.

title: Runtime digest drift
blurb: Sencho notices when a tag has moved: it compares what each node runs with the image digest approved for the Blueprint, per service and platform. Enforce repairs the drift by redeploying the approved content, without pulling from a registry.

title: Whole-project recovery generations
blurb: Protected deploys and updates capture a recovery generation of the whole authored project: compose files, overrides, discoverable include and extends inputs, and env files. Roll back from the stack editor; Resources → Rollback lists each generation and how long it is kept.

title: Secrets in Git with SOPS and age
blurb: Keep sensitive env files in your repository as SOPS-encrypted documents. Sencho generates an age identity on the owning node and decrypts only while a validation, apply, deploy, or rollback needs the values.

title: Private repositories and Git-host webhooks
blurb: Connect private repositories with an SSH deploy key, trust your own certificate authority for a self-hosted Git host, and let GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, or Bitbucket Cloud trigger a pull with a signed webhook from the Automation tab.

title: Stack Health across every node
blurb: Keep Stack Health on This node, or switch to All nodes for a multi-node inventory with state, networks, and coverage. Editor jumps land on the node that owns the stack.

title: Your layout follows you
blurb: Appearance and navigation choices are saved to your account, so your layout is the same in every browser. Pin up to ten quick links to the Compact launcher, and switch the stacks sidebar to Resizable to set its width.

title: Resolve findings where you see them
blurb: Most Readiness findings carry a button that fixes them on the spot, and a finding you have decided to live with can be dismissed until it changes. Networking and Drift findings can be dismissed the same way.

title: Git-managed Blueprints end to end
blurb: Run one Git repository across several nodes. Convert a Git source onto a Blueprint, then accept source, approve placement, and authorize rollout as separate steps, with pause, resume, and rollback along the way.

title: GitOps portfolio
blurb: One place for every Git-managed application across your nodes. The attention queue resolves in place, so a failed source, a pending review, or a held rollout ends in the action that clears it.
